f1.quote: The WTaTiVZr alloy was synthesized by arc melting and remelted at least five times, then its phase constitution, microstructure, compressive behavior, temperature-dependent indentation response, and scratch-based fracture toughness were measured and compared with commercially used pure tungsten.

f2.quote: Room-temperature uniaxial compression used 4 mm × 4 mm cylindrical specimens at an engineering strain rate of 0.001 s^-1.

f3.quote: Indentation plastometry used 5 mm cubes, a 1 mm-radius Si3N4 indenter, loads up to 5 kN, and temperatures from room temperature to 500 °C in 100 °C increments.

f4.quote: Scratch testing used a 200 µm-radius Rockwell C diamond stylus under a constant 100 N normal load at 0.01 mm/s over 3 mm

f6.quote: Solid solution hardening due to severe lattice distortion

f10.quote: showing ~6% room-temperature plastic strain, quasi-cleavage fracture

f11.quote: radial indentation cracks from 25 to 200 °C; indentation cracking was absent above 200 °C

f12.quote: less scratch-induced cracking and damage, and higher fracture toughness
